Conversations within Defence and Peace Economics

1997–2026 catalogue coverage · run 20261015T200742Z-ba31b8f5

1,221 catalogue records; 1,143 eligible papers; 3,097 observed directed links; 3,093 DOI-only links; 188 papers with no observed internal links.

Method

Adapted from Delahais and Thyrard, Conversations in Evaluation and its public replication script. RePEc supplies the article universe; Crossref supplies references. No Scopus data are used.

One node per RePEc handle; one edge from citing to cited paper. Repeated references are deduplicated and article self-loops removed. Shared authors do not remove an edge. Editorials, issue introductions, administrative records, corrections and routine book notices are excluded. Substantive reviews remain eligible. Every decision is preserved in evidence.json.

DOIs are normalized and identities checked against metadata. Unique exact bibliographic matches use journal, volume, first page and author surname, or exact title and surname. Ambiguities require documented review; fuzzy matches are not automatically accepted. The recovered graph is accompanied by a DOI-only baseline. Recovered links and DOI corrections are audited before publication.

Louvain communities are computed on an undirected projection, summing reciprocal edge weights. Resolution 1; seeds 0–19; maximum modularity with deterministic tie-breaking. Selected seed 5, modularity 0.6486. Resolutions 0.5 and 1.5 are sensitivity checks. NetworkX 3.6.1. ForceAtlas2 seed 42, 500 iterations within each component; disconnected components are packed at the right and isolated papers below. Their relative placement is arbitrary. All discovered communities are retained.

Limits and denominators

Pre-1997 papers are outside this catalogue. Publication years follow RePEc issue years, which can differ from first-online dates. 2026 and end periods reflect catalogue availability. Missing Crossref deposits and unmatched references can remove genuine edges; no observed link does not establish no citation. Citations do not establish agreement or substantive intellectual exchange. Community labels describe reviewed leading titles and available abstracts.

Temporal shares use all eligible papers in a period, including papers without observed links; pooled communities remain fixed. Topic comparisons use all eligible community members, with missing and unassigned abstracts reported separately. The bound topic run is 20261015T200740Z-e4c83645.

Network

Communities

  1. Military spending and economic growth (139 articles): Leading papers debate growth-model specification and estimate heterogeneous economic effects of military spending using panel and country evidence.
  2. Defence industries and European procurement (135 articles): Leading papers connect European defence policy, industrial collaboration, weapons costs and procurement efficiency.
  3. Terrorism, counterterrorism and economic effects (134 articles): Leading papers examine terrorist recruitment, the effects of deterrence and political policies, and the economic costs of terrorism.
  4. Demand for military expenditure (117 articles): Leading papers estimate military-spending demand and distinguish economic determinants, strategic threats and spillovers.
  5. Arms markets, technology and capability (81 articles): Leading papers combine strategic arms trade, defence R&D, equipment quality and asymmetric arms-race models; the scope is broader than arms exports alone.
  6. Geopolitical risk, resources and markets (71 articles): Leading papers address geopolitical-risk measures, financial-market responses and resource-related military spending; this is a mixed empirical community.
  7. Defence spending, debt and public budgets (70 articles): Leading papers study external debt, government budget choices and interactions between military and welfare expenditure.
  8. Military recruitment, retention and conscription (37 articles): Leading papers analyse enlistment incentives, pilot retention and changes from conscription to volunteer forces.
  9. Civil war and the economic costs of conflict (36 articles): Leading papers review civil-war research and estimate direct, regional and neighbouring-country consequences of armed conflict.
  10. Third-party intervention and conflict bargaining (30 articles): Leading papers use strategic conflict models to examine intervention, rebellion, territorial disputes and bargaining.
  11. Greek–Turkish military rivalry (24 articles): Leading papers review Greek–Turkish arms-race evidence and link military spending to strategic threats and Greek economic performance.
  12. Aircraft replacement and defence inflation (15 articles): Leading papers develop economic replacement rules for ageing aircraft and relate equipment costs to defence inflation.
  13. Valuing defence and security preferences (7 articles): Leading papers consider the welfare case for defence, individual preferences, national-security utility and business-cycle models.
  14. Risk, insurance and emergency provision (4 articles): Leading papers model supply interruptions, risk aversion, insurance and international public goods.
  15. Conflict exposure, education and economic growth (4 articles): This small group connects schooling, child labour and gender differences in education with a study of violence and economic growth in Colombia.
  16. Armoured vehicles and casualty cost-effectiveness (4 articles): This small group includes an explicit published exchange over the data and methods used to evaluate armoured tactical vehicles, together with a linked casualty-care study.
  17. Terrorism research and prevention methods (3 articles): This small group links a taxonomy of terrorism research, a study of predictability before 9/11 and evaluation of camera surveillance. The links alone do not establish one sustained debate.
  18. Illicit small arms and ammunition markets (3 articles): Leading papers trace illicit small-arms supply chains, ammunition diversion and market prices.
  19. Civil-conflict motives and economic shocks (3 articles): This small group connects greed/grievance arguments, economic shocks and institutional accounts of conflict.
  20. Deployment selection, health and education (3 articles): This small group connects selection into deployment with mental health and educational outcomes of deployment and combat.
  21. French First World War military casualties (3 articles): Leading papers use French historical soldier records to study deaths and military executions.
  22. Israeli–Palestinian bargaining and proxy conflict (3 articles): Leading papers model monopolization of violence, proxy-war relationships and obstacles to negotiated resolution.
  23. Militant groups, rivalry and targeting (3 articles): Leading papers connect militant-group ethnicity and rivalry with rebel decisions to target Americans.
  24. Military organization and battlefield performance (2 articles): Two linked papers examine battlefield success and the effects of military unionization. This small pair is a connection rather than evidence of a broad community.
  25. Narcotics, crime and security policy (2 articles): Two linked papers model narcotics restrictions and connect international crime with European threat perceptions.
  26. Civil-war termination and political outcomes (2 articles): Two linked papers study how civil wars end and the political consequences of different outcomes.
  27. Iraq mortality-survey controversy (2 articles): Two linked articles scrutinize the methods, integrity and corroboration of the second Lancet Iraq mortality survey. This label describes the papers’ subjects without adjudicating their claims.
  28. Economic growth and interstate war (2 articles): Two linked papers examine whether economic growth increases the likelihood of interstate conflict.
  29. Swedish military service and later earnings (2 articles): Two linked studies estimate civilian earnings effects of military training and peacekeeping deployment in Sweden.
  30. Nuclear deterrence and defensive weapons (2 articles): Two linked game-theoretic papers examine nuclear acquisition, deterrence and the consequences of asymmetric defensive shields.
  31. Armed violence and economic development (2 articles): Two linked papers address resource dependence, sustainability and the effects of civil war on financial development.
  32. Corruption and procurement accountability (2 articles): Two linked papers model corruption controls and the costs and benefits of procurement bid protests.
  33. Espionage and innovation contests (2 articles): Two linked theoretical papers study economic espionage, copying and competition over innovative effort.
  34. Orbital debris and space security (2 articles): Two linked papers examine space debris, behavioural incentives and the consequences of anti-satellite weapons.
  35. House raids, demolitions and conflict behaviour (2 articles): Two linked studies examine household exposure to state coercion and claims about punitive demolitions and suicide bombing. The label does not establish agreement between them.
  36. Commodity shocks, conflict and peacekeeping (2 articles): Two linked empirical papers examine commodity-price shocks, conflict intensity and the possible buffering role of UN peacekeeping.
